questions.stem: Choose the exact correct synonym for the word: BEAUTIFUL
questions.explanation: 'Beautiful' means pleasing the senses or mind aesthetically. 'Gorgeous' shares this meaning, meaning beautiful or very attractive.

questions.stem: Choose the exact correct synonym for the word: QUICK
questions.explanation: 'Quick' means moving fast or doing something in a short time. 'Fast' is its direct synonym.

questions.stem: Choose the exact correct synonym for the word: OBSTINATE
questions.explanation: 'Obstinate' means stubbornly refusing to change one's opinion or chosen course of action. 'Stubborn' is its perfect synonym.

questions.stem: Choose the exact correct synonym for the formal word: PROLIFIC
questions.explanation: To be 'prolific' means producing much fruit or foliage or many offspring, or present in large numbers or quantities. 'Productive' accurately captures this meaning.

questions.stem: Choose the exact correct synonym for the word: COGENT
questions.explanation: An argument or case that is 'cogent' is clear, logical, and convincing. Therefore, 'Convincing' is the correct synonym.

questions.stem: Choose the exact correct synonym for the formal word: TREPIDATION
questions.explanation: 'Trepidation' is a feeling of fear or agitation about something that may happen. 'Apprehension' is its closest synonym.

questions.stem: Choose the exact correct synonym for the literary word: PERFIDIOUS
questions.explanation: 'Perfidious' means deceitful and untrustworthy. 'Treacherous' accurately captures this meaning of betrayal.

questions.stem: The countryside retreat was described as 'serene'. Which of the following is the closest synonym of 'serene'?

options.option_text: loud and very difficult to control
sharp and cutting in its manner

questions.explanation: 'Serene' means calm, peaceful and untroubled — 'calm and undisturbed in character' matches precisely. 'Rushing forward with restless energy' (option C) is the most tempting wrong answer for those who confuse 'serene' with 'keen'; it is actually the antonym in spirit.

questions.stem: A 'diligent' employee is best described as someone who is —

options.option_text: speaking rudely and without careful thought
moving very slowly without any purpose
working hard and with steady care
pretending to work while avoiding tasks

questions.explanation: 'Diligent' means hardworking, careful and persistent — 'working hard and with steady care' is the correct synonym. Option D (pretending to work) describes the very opposite behaviour and is the classic distractor for candidates who conflate 'diligent' with 'dilatory'.

questions.stem: The victorious general was praised for being 'magnanimous' toward the defeated troops. Which word is closest in meaning to 'magnanimous'?

options.option_text: deeply suspicious of the enemy's motives
proud and unwilling to forgive wrongs

questions.explanation: 'Magnanimous' (Latin: magnus = great + animus = spirit) means nobly generous, especially in forgiving — 'generous and forgiving toward others' is correct. Option C ('proud and unwilling to forgive') is the most tempting wrong choice as it sounds grand but is actually closer to 'arrogant' or 'vindictive'.

questions.stem: He was a 'taciturn' man who rarely spoke even at family gatherings. Which option best captures the meaning of 'taciturn'?

options.option_text: known for long and passionate speeches
enthusiastic and expressive on every topic

questions.explanation: 'Taciturn' (Latin: tacere = to be silent) means habitually reserved or uncommunicative — 'speaking very little by nature' is the precise synonym. Option B is the antonym; option C describes an 'orator'. Candidates sometimes confuse 'taciturn' with 'tactful', which has an entirely different meaning.

questions.stem: Poets often lament the 'ephemeral' nature of youth and beauty. Which of the following is the best synonym for 'ephemeral'?

options.option_text: lasting only for a very brief time
deeply rooted in an ancient tradition
growing steadily stronger each passing year

questions.explanation: 'Ephemeral' (Greek: epi + hemera = lasting a day) means short-lived or transitory — 'lasting only for a very brief time' is correct. Options A and D are antonyms that describe permanence; option C misleadingly suggests historical depth, trapping candidates who link 'ephemeral' with things of the past.

questions.stem: The professor's 'recondite' lecture on medieval manuscript traditions attracted only a handful of scholars. Which option is closest in meaning to 'recondite'?

options.option_text: simple enough for any child to grasp
obscure and known to very few
easily understood by most ordinary readers

questions.explanation: 'Recondite' means dealing with abstruse or little-known subject matter, beyond ordinary understanding — 'obscure and known to very few' is the synonym. Options B and D are near-antonyms. Option A ('widely popular') is the most tempting wrong answer because candidates sometimes associate 'recondite' with 'recognised', sharing a similar sound.

questions.stem: Ernest Hemingway's celebrated 'laconic' prose left much unsaid yet communicated everything. Which option most accurately gives the meaning of 'laconic'?

options.option_text: expressing a great deal in very few words
writing in elaborate and highly ornate style
repeating the same ideas in different phrasing
speaking at unnecessary length without clear aim

questions.explanation: 'Laconic' derives from Laconia (Sparta), whose inhabitants were famously brief in speech; it means terse yet meaningful — 'expressing a great deal in very few words' is correct. Option B ('elaborate and ornate') describes the polar opposite style, i.e., 'verbose' or 'grandiloquent'. Option D ('speaking at unnecessary length') describes 'prolix', a commonly confused term in SSC/IBPS vocabulary questions.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the closest synonym of 'SERENE' as used in the phrase 'a serene disposition'?

options.option_text: angry and easily provoked by others

questions.explanation: SERENE means calm, peaceful, and free from disturbance — 'peaceful and undisturbed in manner' captures this precisely. 'Restless and deeply troubled' is the most tempting wrong choice as it sounds introspective, but it is actually the antonym of serene. 'Noisy' and 'angry' are clearly opposite in meaning.

questions.stem: Select the best synonym for 'DILIGENT' as used in the sentence: 'She was a diligent worker who never missed a deadline'?

options.option_text: reckless and hasty in every step

questions.explanation: DILIGENT means showing steady, careful, and persistent effort — 'hardworking and careful in duties' is the correct match. 'Reckless and hasty' is the most tempting distractor because it implies speed, which students sometimes confuse with efficiency, but diligent specifically implies care and thoroughness, not speed.

questions.stem: Which of the following best captures the meaning of 'LACONIC' in the sentence: 'His laconic reply left everyone puzzled'?

options.option_text: using very few words to express

questions.explanation: LACONIC (derived from Laconia, home of the Spartans, who were famous for brevity) means expressing much in few words. 'Using very few words to express' is correct. The common trap is 'deeply emotional and quite sentimental' — students confuse laconic with lachrymose (tearful). 'Talkative and long-winded' is the direct antonym.

questions.stem: Choose the correct synonym for 'MOLLIFY' as used in the sentence: 'The manager tried to mollify the irate customer'?

options.option_text: to soothe and calm rising anger

questions.explanation: MOLLIFY means to appease or reduce the anger of someone — 'to soothe and calm rising anger' is correct. 'To aggravate and intensify hostility' is the antonym and a frequent distractor. 'To delay and postpone' is a trap for students who confuse mollify with stall or defer; the word has no association with postponement.

questions.stem: Identify the synonym of 'OSTENTATIOUS' as used in the context: 'He made an ostentatious display of his new wealth'?

options.option_text: showy and designed to impress others
harsh and unpleasantly blunt in speech

questions.explanation: OSTENTATIOUS means characterized by a vulgar or pretentious display intended to impress — 'showy and designed to impress others' is the exact match. 'Modest and deliberately understated' is the antonym and a trap for students who mix up ostentatious with ostensible (apparent/seeming). 'Secretive' is the opposite of the word's core meaning of conspicuous display.

questions.stem: The historian's work was praised for its recondite scholarship. Which word is the closest synonym of 'RECONDITE'?

options.option_text: obscure and understood by very few
vivid and strikingly clear in form

questions.explanation: RECONDITE means abstruse or known only to the learned — 'obscure and understood by very few' is correct. 'Vivid and strikingly clear' is the most dangerous distractor: students who guess from context that a praised scholar must write clearly choose this, but recondite specifically praises depth and rarity of knowledge, not clarity. 'Practical and easily applied' describes the opposite register of knowledge.

questions.stem: The new regulations were criticised as being inimical to the interests of micro-enterprises. Choose the correct synonym of 'INIMICAL'?

options.option_text: hostile and deeply harmful to interests

questions.explanation: INIMICAL means tending to obstruct or harm; adverse and hostile — 'hostile and deeply harmful to interests' is the precise match. 'Neutral and wholly indifferent' is the subtlest trap: students who half-recall that inimical has a negative connotation but confuse it with neutral or non-committal choose this. Inimical specifically implies active opposition or harm, not mere indifference. 'Friendly' is the antonym.
